title: You Could Win $14,000 for Sleeping in Tokyo
paragraphs: Would you like to win money for sleeping? In Tokyo, one person did exactly that. A sleeping contest gave its winner a prize of 2 million yen, or about $14,000.
The contest was called the "Matt Race." It was organized by Koala, a company that makes mattresses, and it was held in Tokyo on October 5, 2026.

People had to apply to take part. According to one report, the contest received about 47,000 applications. Only a small number of people were chosen. There were three races, with about 20 people in each race.

During each race, the people lay down on mattresses in a dark room and tried to sleep for up to 90 minutes. They wore special devices that measured their sleep. The winner was the person who fell asleep the fastest and slept the most deeply. People were not allowed to take sleeping pills or anything else to help them sleep.
The winner was a woman who used the nickname "Suimii." She said she would use the prize money to pay for moving to a new home and to buy a princess-style bed.

Riichiro Nakama, who helped plan the event, said Japan is often described as a country where people do not get enough sleep. He hoped the contest would make people more interested in sleep. According to OECD data from 2021, Japanese people slept an average of 7 hours and 24 minutes a day, the least among the countries compared.
One participant, Chisato Honda, 32, said the race was over in an instant, and that she wished she could have slept a little longer.
